title: Advanced Attribution D1 — Data-driven attribution
caption:
Last click gives all the credit to the final step.
The Meta ad and the Google search that started the journey get nothing.

Data-driven attribution in GA4 works differently
→ It compares paths that converted with paths that didn't
→ It gives more credit to the steps that changed the outcome
→ It keeps learning as your data grows

GA4 has three reporting models
1. Data-driven
2. Paid and organic last click
3. Google paid channels last click

Change it in Admin → Attribution settings. Reports use the new model for past data too.

title: Advanced Attribution D6 — Incrementality
caption:
Attribution shows who was there. It doesn't prove who caused the sale.

Incrementality asks a different question: would this sale have happened without the ad?

1. Split people or regions into two groups
2. Show ads to one group only
3. Compare sales between the two
4. The difference is the real lift

Meta and Google Ads offer lift studies for eligible accounts. You can also run a geo test yourself.

title: More Advanced Attribution D1 — Click IDs
caption:
Your ads lose click IDs before the page even loads.

Every ad platform adds an ID to your landing URL: gclid, gbraid and wbraid for Google Ads, fbclid for Meta, ttclid for TikTok, msclkid for Microsoft.

Lose it, and the sale can't be tied back to the ad.

How it gets lost
→ Redirects that drop the query string
→ The ID isn't saved before the visitor moves on
→ Forms and CRMs never receive it

The fix
1. Check every redirect keeps the URL parameters
2. Save the IDs in a first-party cookie
3. Pass them into hidden form fields and your CRM
4. Send them back with offline uploads or the Conversions API

title: More Advanced Attribution D2 — Cookie lifetime & server-side
caption:
Safari can expire JavaScript cookies after 7 days.
Visitor clicks your ad on day 1, buys on day 10, and the sale goes to "direct".

The fix: set cookies from your own server
→ Run server-side GTM on a subdomain of your own site, like "data."
→ The cookie is set with a Set-Cookie header, not JavaScript
→ Use your main domain, not a provider's default URL

Then test in Safari, not only in Chrome. Safari can still limit cookies if the tagging server's IP is very different from your website's.

title: GTM Advanced D1

GTM can't see inside iframes.

Booking widgets, embedded forms and payment pages often run on another domain. Your GTM container can't read what happens inside, so bookings and leads go missing.

→ Always check the message origin before you trust it
→ Push one clean event to the data layer

Widget sends nothing? Redirect to a thank-you page on your domain, or use the tool's webhook to send a server event.

title: GTM Advanced D3
caption:
Send profit, not just revenue.

A big order with a small margin looks great to your ads. A small order with a big margin looks worse.

With server-side GTM you can fix that
→ The browser sends the purchase as usual
→ Your server looks up each product's margin, for example with a Firestore Lookup variable
→ Ad platforms get the profit value, and your margins never appear in the browser

The 10-point Stape audit
1. Custom domain, ideally same origin
2. Custom Loader on
3. Cookie Keeper for key cookies
4. One clear data path per event
5. Browser and server events deduplicated
6. Consent passed and respected on the server
7. Bot traffic filtered
8. Logs checked after every publish
9. Monitoring alerts on
10. Request usage reviewed monthly

9–10: strong. 6–8: fix the gaps. 0–5: your data and ad spend are at risk.
